# AlgoViz

> AlgoViz is a free, browser-based learning tool for stepping through JavaScript and C++ code and visualizing data structures and algorithms.

AlgoViz is intended for students, educators, and developers who want to inspect how a program changes as it runs. Users can write or paste code, run it, then step through execution while inspecting variables, console output, call stacks, and supported structure diagrams.

## Product facts

- Supported languages: JavaScript (ES6+) and C++. C++ support is labeled beta in the app.
- JavaScript execution runs in the browser. C++ compilation uses WebAssembly in the browser.
- Visualizations include arrays and matrices, linked lists, trees, stacks, queues, heaps, hash maps, and graphs when the runtime state can be recognized.
- The template library includes examples for searching, sorting, recursion, graph traversal, and other data-structure and algorithm topics.
- Time and space complexity panels provide pattern-based estimates for learning. They are not proofs or substitutes for analyzing worst-case behavior.
- The app is free to use and does not require an account. The source code is public on GitHub.
- Shared session links encode source code in the URL fragment. Users should review code before sharing a link.
